method: Inclusion is every species printed under the Sciuridae heading on the 2011 Wayback SANParks KNP mammal checklist PDF (1 species). English and Afrikaans names, and species order, are taken from that PDF. Scientific names are the 2011 names unless an iNaturalist taxon record cited in remaps gives a current name. Research-grade counts are for iNaturalist place_id 69020. iNaturalist-only sciurids are in candidates, not species. The PDF was fetched to a temporary path for text extraction and was not copied into this project.

sources.role: Official inclusion list; English and Afrikaans species names; species order; absence of asterisk status flags on Sciuridae
Research-grade species counts for Sciuridae in Kruger (place 69020); 1 species in this pull (Paraxerus cepapi, 1008). Paraxerus palliatus was absent from this pull.
All-grade Sciuridae taxonomy tree for place 69020; used to find iNat-only Paraxerus palliatus and subspecies identifications P. c. cepapi and P. c. carpi
total_results for candidate Paraxerus palliatus (taxon 46113, 0 research-grade, 3 of any grade)
Current name lists for Paraxerus cepapi and Paraxerus palliatus; the 2011 scientific name of the official species is unchanged

remaps.note: iNaturalist preferred_common_name for taxon 46110. The 2011 name is not a listed English name on this taxon. Yellow-footed Squirrel is a listed English name. The stored en value is the 2011 SANParks checklist name.

notes: iNaturalist-only in place 69020: 0 research-grade and 3 observations of any grade (taxon 46113; preferred_common_name Red Bush Squirrel). Not on the 2011 SANParks Sciuridae list, which has Tree squirrel as Paraxerus cepapi only. Left in candidates, not included.

gaps: Live SANParks checklist HTML and PDF were not fetched in this session (Phase 1 recorded HTTP 403). Inclusion is the 2011 Wayback PDF only, and has not been compared with the live 147–148 figure.
iNaturalist checklist 8810 was not fetched (Phase 1 recorded HTTP 403/401).

Paraxerus palliatus is an iNaturalist-only species in the place (0 research-grade, 3 of any grade). It is a separate active iNaturalist species, not a synonym of P. cepapi, so it was not used to remap the official tree squirrel.
Subspecies identifications of the included species (Paraxerus cepapi cepapi, Paraxerus cepapi carpi) were not treated as separate candidates, because the 2011 list is at species rank.
Candidate Afrikaans names were left null. The Phase 2 rule was to take af from the 2011 SANParks checklist; these taxa are not on that list.

No rare, reintroduced, or introduced flags are recorded for official Sciuridae species: the 2011 PDF does not mark any of them with an asterisk or other status note (asterisks on that list are only for house mouse and house/black rat under Muridae).
The current live official list, Skinner & Chimimba, and Stuart's guide were not available to corroborate remaps or flags.
